k0s follows the upstream Kubernetes release model: each minor is maintained for roughly 14 months from its initial release; Mirantis sells commercial support that adds critical security patches for versions outside the open-source window

k0s backup/restore archives the etcd or Kine/SQLite snapshot plus k0s-managed config on a controller node and restores it with 'k0s restore'; there is no atomic rollback of the Kubernetes layer beyond restoring a snapshot

k0s ADOPTERS.md (production users) lists AudioCodes (VoIP/VoiceAI product), Defense Unicorns (Unified Defense Stack for mission environments), logsight/exalsius (geo-distributed GPU clusters), DeepSquare (HPCaaS), KubeArmor and Mirantis among others

k0s Autopilot updates controller and worker nodes in place from a declarative Plan (kubectl apply) and can do automatic updates via an UpdateConfig object; the public update server exposes one edge_release channel
canonical/microk8s LICENSE at release v1.36 is Apache-2.0

MicroK8s upgrading docs: patch releases update automatically within the installed channel; a minor upgrade is an explicit channel refresh; if an upgrade fails the node is reverted by hand with 'sudo snap revert microk8s'; the page states no support duration per channel
MicroK8s high availability is enabled automatically with three or more nodes, which keep copies of the dqlite datastore; the HA page states no memory or footprint requirement

Moby BRANCHES-AND-TAGS: docker-29.x is Maintained until 'After docker-30.x' (distributors Docker, Microsoft); 25.0 is Maintained to 2026-12-04 (Amazon, Mirantis); 28.x and older are Unmaintained; the status is 'informational and not binding'; no fixed support period is published

Docker docs, Install on Debian: supports Debian 13 and 12 on x86_64, armhf, arm64 and ppc64le; the apt repository is signed (Signed-By key); upgrading means re-running install step 2 with the new version (in place)
containers/podman LICENSE at v6.2.0 is Apache-2.0
podman auto-update --rollback (default true): if restarting the systemd unit after an image update fails, Podman rolls back to the previous image and restarts the unit

Flight Control (shipping, Apache-2.0) manages Podman container workloads (docker-compose, Quadlets) and MicroShift workloads on bootc/ostree devices, and itself deploys as Quadlets or the flightctl-services RPM
Velero v1.18.4 LICENSE is Apache-2.0 and its release assets include linux-amd64, linux-arm64 and linux-arm binaries
Velero support process: best-effort community support for the current and n-1 minor versions (all patch releases), run by a weekly maintainer rotation; no dated support window

Longhorn release policy (wiki): from 1.8, a 4-month minor cadence, 2-month best-effort patch cadence and on-demand monthly security patches; each minor gets 6 months of active support from x.y.1, and community support for x.y ends when x.(y+1).1 is released

OpenZFS RELEASES.md at zfs-2.4.4: LTS releases receive patches for at least 2 years and newer kernels are not supported on them; the current LTS is OpenZFS 2.2; the 'current' branch stops maintaining the previous minor when a new one is tagged
borgmatic (third-party automation wrapper for borg) released 2.2.0 on 2026-10-29 and is GPL-3.0 (GitHub licence API at the tag)

SWUpdate documentation 'Update images from verified source': SWUpdate verifies incoming images against a known source and documents signing the sub-images (sw-description) rather than the whole compound image

Mender standalone deployment: with no Mender Server, 'mender-update install <URI>' installs an Artifact from file storage (for example a USB stick path) or HTTP/HTTPS, and 'mender-update commit' marks it successful and permanent
meta-raspberrypi defines a raspberrypi5 machine (Cortex-A76 tune, bcm2712 device trees for Pi 5 B and CM5 on CM5IO/CM4IO, kernel_2712.img)
Canonical (2020-02-19): 'Bosch Rexroth has selected Ubuntu Core for their app-based platform ctrlX AUTOMATION', with apps delivered as snaps

Bosch Rexroth ctrlX OS page: ctrlX OS is a Linux-based, hardware-independent OS currently available on the ctrlX CORE control platform and the ctrlX DRIVE drive system, with Canonical providing security, support and customisation services; the page itself does not name Ubuntu Core [status note: links the shipping product to Canonical; the Ubuntu Core base rests on the 2020 Canonical announcement]

AlmaLinux/bootc-images-rpi README: AlmaLinux bootc images for Raspberry Pi are 'experimental'; tested on several rpi5 versions (2g, 8g, 16g), rpi4, rpi3 and rpi zero 2 w; GPT image for RPI5/RPI4, flashable to m.2 (RPI5 only), SD or USB; firmware updating may need manual steps or a reimage
